## TL;DR - October 24: conference at Ville Ponti in Varese - At 10 the research on cross-border workers - Two round tables on the economy and institutions - Conclusions at 12.30 with Mattia Pirulli
## Key facts - When → Saturday, October 24, from 9.30 - Where → Centro Congressi Varese «Ville Ponti» - Research → «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers» - Promoters → Cisl dei Laghi, Cisl Piemonte Orientale, Cisl Sondrio, Ocst and BiblioLavoro - Topics → economic impact on the local area and the role of institutions
On October 24, from 9.30, Centro Congressi Varese «Ville Ponti» will host the conference dedicated to cross-border work and its impact on the local area. The event is promoted by Cisl dei Laghi, Cisl Piemonte Orientale, Cisl Sondrio, Ocst and BiblioLavoro.
### The research opens the proceedings
At 10, Francesco Girolimetto, director of BiblioLavoro, will present the research «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers». The program places the study at the center of the morning, before the discussion on the local economy and the role of institutions.
The opening remarks will be delivered by Dino Perboni, regional secretary of Cisl Lombardia. After this address, the conference will move on to the first roundtable, dedicated to the impact of cross-border work on the local economy.
The discussion will involve Andrea Puglia, deputy cantonal secretary of Ocst; Michele Rossi of the Chamber of Commerce of the Canton of Ticino; Mauro Vitiello, president of the Chamber of Commerce of Varese; and Elena Ugazio, general secretary of Cisl Piemonte Orientale. Matteo Inzaghi, director of Rete 55, will moderate.
### Two roundtables, two topics
At 11, the discussion will focus on the action of institutions in support of cross-border work. Participants will include Marco Contessa, Cisl's national head for cross-border workers; Massimo Sertori, Lombardy regional councillor; Massimo Mastromarino, president of the Association of Border Municipalities; and Luca Della Bitta, mayor of Chiavenna. Journalist Anna Campaniello will moderate.
The closing remarks, scheduled for 12.30, will be delivered by Mattia Pirulli, national secretary of Cisl. The source presents the morning as structured around research dedicated to cross-border workers, a discussion on the local economy and a focus on the institutions involved in cross-border work. ## The programme compares two levels
The programme offers a concrete comparison between the research perspective and two areas of discussion. It does not anticipate the study's conclusions: it indicates that the research will be presented at 10 and that, subsequently, cross-border work will be examined first through the local economy and then through institutions. This sequence is the comparable element provided by the source.
### The sequence of events
| Time | Content | Stated focus | |---|---|---| | 10 | Presentation of the research | Conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers | | Following this | First round table | Impact of cross-border work on the local economy | | 11 | Second round table | Role of institutions in promoting cross-border work | | 12.30 | Conclusions | Mattia Pirulli, national secretary of Cisl |
The first discussion focuses on the local area. The presence on the same panel of representatives of the Chamber of Commerce of the Canton of Ticino and Varese, together with representatives of Cisl and Ocst, places side by side the parties identified in the source to discuss the economic impact. However, the content of their positions is not indicated, nor are economic data or estimates provided.
The second discussion shifts level and considers the role of institutions: the programme brings together a national head of Frontalieri Cisl, a regional councillor from Lombardy, the president of the Associazione Comuni di Frontiera and the mayor of Chiavenna. The source defines the topic, namely the possible institutional role in promoting cross-border work, but does not announce measures, proposals or decisions.
Taken as a whole, the agenda distinguishes three stages: the presentation of a study, the dialogue on the local economy and the section on institutions. The stated schedule runs from 9.30 to 12.30: that is three hours in total when considering the interval between the start and the conclusions. The calculation describes only the theoretical duration of the event and does not say how much time will be devoted to each contribution. ## The scope of the announcement
The available text primarily documents the organization of the meeting, not the outcome of the research. The news item specifies the title of the study, the speaker, the organizers, the times and the participants, but does not report the results that will be presented at 10. The wording “conclusions” also indicates who will close the proceedings, without anticipating the content of the final presentation.
### What remains to be verified
The program does not specify whether the research will address operational aspects such as the G permit or withholding tax. The available text contains no references to AVS, LPP and LAMal, nor to rebates. INPS, the Brogeda border crossing or double taxation are not mentioned in the published program either.
These limitations make it impossible, based solely on the announcement, to attribute to the conference a discussion of tax rules, social security, health insurance, commutes or relations with Italian institutions. Instead, the source speaks in general terms of the conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers, assigning the research the task of bringing these issues to the center of the morning’s proceedings.
According to the roles indicated, the program involves national, regional, cantonal and municipal levels. The names of the participants document the composition of the discussions, but do not amount to statements or positions already expressed. No agreements, shared requests or developments following the event are announced.
The verifiable news therefore remains the presentation on October 24 at Ville Ponti in Varese and the structure of the conference: research on cross-border workers, a roundtable on the local economy, a second on the role of institutions, and the conclusions entrusted to Mattia Pirulli. Any assessment of the study’s results or possible proposals remains outside the available text.

item.description: 1.542 responses collected in May 2026 31,7% over an hour and a half commuting 87,8% considers the «health tax» penalizing 76,9% does not assess
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 1.542 responses collected in May 2026 - 31,7% spend more than an hour and a half commuting - 87,8% consider the “health tax” detrimental - 76,9% are not considering moving to Switzerland
## Key facts - Research → «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers» - Promoters → CISL dei Laghi, CISL Sondrio, CISL Piemonte Orientale and OCST - Responses → 1.542 online questionnaires in May 2026 - Presentation → Saturday, October 24 at 9.30 - Venue → Ville Ponti Congress Center in Varese - Como → almost 32 thousand cross-border workers - Varese → 31 thousand cross-border workers - Share from Como → 41% of Italian workers employed in Ticino
### The questionnaire and the presentation In May 2026, 1.542 workers responded to the online questionnaire promoted by CISL dei Laghi, CISL Sondrio, CISL Piemonte Orientale and the Ticino trade union OCST. The research, entitled «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers», will be presented on Saturday, October 24 at 9.30 at the Ville Ponti Congress Center in Varese.
The stated aim is to collect information directly from cross-border workers about changes in their work, without limiting itself to official statistics, and to turn what is heard into concrete proposals. Scientific coordination is entrusted to BiblioLavoro, the study center of CISL Lombardia.
The research concerns tens of thousands of people: every morning they cross the border to get to work in Switzerland, and every evening they make the reverse journey to return home. Almost 32 thousand cross-border workers depart from the province of Como, accounting for 41% of Italian workers employed in Ticino; another 31 thousand depart from the province of Varese.
Daily commuting is one of the first elements measured by the survey:
> «Almost one worker in three (31,7%) spends more than an hour and a half each day commuting between home and work; for 73,2% of respondents, the main means of transport is a private car.»
As for flexibility, only 37,4% of respondents work for companies that allow cross-border workers to use teleworking. The questionnaire thus places side by side the time spent commuting, the use of private cars and the still limited availability of remote work, offering an initial snapshot of the conditions reported by those who work across the border in the Canton of Ticino. ## Salary, purchasing power and employee benefits
### Three levels of the same snapshot The pay data do not yield a single assessment. 73% of respondents say they are satisfied with their salary, while 48,4% perceive a decline in their purchasing power in recent years. The two percentages refer to different dimensions: the first measures satisfaction with pay, while the second measures the perception of how it has evolved over time. Taken together, they show a gap between satisfaction with salary and the perceived trend in purchasing power, without the survey attributing this gap to a specific cause.
| Dimension | Questionnaire result | |---|---| | Salary comparison | 55,6% consider their pay lower than that of a Swiss resident performing the same duties | | Collective agreement | The share rises to 63,4% among those without coverage | | Discriminatory treatment | 42,7% report at least one incident they perceived as discriminatory because they are cross-border workers | | Employee benefits | 58,9% are not satisfied |
The change from 55,6% to 63,4% is presented by the source as a difference between all respondents and those without collective-agreement coverage. The survey provides no other information to explain that gap, but indicates a perception of earning less than a Swiss resident performing the same duties. The 42,7% point to a second concern: they report at least one incident in which they considered the treatment they received discriminatory because they were a cross-border worker.
Employee benefits also receive a clear-cut assessment. For the majority, there are no transport allowances, meal vouchers or production bonuses, while 58,9% say they are not satisfied with them. The so-called “health tax” is considered detrimental by 87,8% of respondents.
Finally, a need for information emerges regarding the second pillar: 69,2% say they have little or no knowledge of how their pension fund works. In the survey, the pension issue is therefore associated primarily with limited knowledge of the system, not with a numerical assessment of future benefits. ## Telework, balance and life choice
### The comparison between remote and on-site work Telework also emerges from the survey as an element for comparing different organizational conditions. Among those who use it, 95,2% endorse it almost unanimously. The assessment therefore concerns workers who already have access to remote work and experience it directly.
The same study then compares work-life balance. Among those who work remotely, 69,5% say they are satisfied; the share drops to 51,8% among those who work exclusively on-site. These percentages refer to two distinct groups in the questionnaire and describe a difference in views on everyday balance, without turning it into a prediction or a causal explanation.
The final indication concerns residential mobility. 76,9% would not consider moving to Switzerland. According to the study, cross-border commuting thus constitutes a stable life choice, rather than a step toward emigration. The figure completes the picture of work across the border: the questionnaire considers employment conditions, commuting, telework and personal prospects together.
After the analysis, the volume devotes its second part to trade union proposals. In the available content, however, the individual proposals are not listed. It is therefore not possible to attribute specific measures to the study beyond the stated aim of turning listening into concrete proposals.
The text provided also does not report data or rules on permit G, AVS, LPP, LAMal, refunds, withholding tax, Brogeda, INPS or double taxation. These topics cannot be derived from the survey percentages and remain outside the analysis described by the source.

item.title: Lugano: parliamentary question on safeguard clause and cross-border workers
item.description: Omar Wicht questions the Municipality of Lugano Regional clause approved in September 2026 Temporary limits on immigration among the measures
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Omar Wicht questions the Lugano Municipal Council - Regional clause approved in September 2026 - Temporary limits on immigration among the measures envisaged - Possible request by Ticino to the Federal Council
## Key facts - Proposer → Omar Wicht, Northern League municipal councilor - Place → Lugano - Instrument → new regional safeguard clause - Base → agreements between Switzerland and the European Union - Threshold → «serious economic or social difficulty» - Measures → temporary limitations and restrictive measures - Recipients → Council of State and Federal Council - Approval indicated → September 2026
Omar Wicht, Northern League municipal councilor, presented a question to the Lugano Municipality. In the text he asks whether the Executive intends to urge the Ticino Government to discuss with the Confederation to evaluate the possible application of the new regional safeguard clause. The source presents the initiative as a question, not as a decision already adopted by the Lugano Executive.
The clause is described as a provision in agreements between Switzerland and the European Union, including agreements on the free movement of persons. According to the explanation given, the provision would allow immigration to be temporarily contained and restrictive measures introduced if the influx of people generates serious economic or social problems. The question recalls a regional clause approved in September 2026.
### The point raised in Lugano Wicht focuses on Lugano, indicated as the economic engine of the Canton. It highlights the strong presence of cross-border workers in the service sector and advanced tertiary sectors. According to the city councilor, this phenomenon negatively affects urban traffic and the level of rents, weighs on the finances of social services and increases the pressure on wages, referred to as wage dumping.
On this basis, the request aims to clarify whether, according to the Lugano Executive, current conditions make intervention necessary. The question is also asked whether the Municipality intends to urge the Council of State to address the Federal Council directly.
The news therefore concerns the transition from a local evaluation to a possible cantonal and federal initiative. It does not yet report the activation of the clause, nor the adoption of restrictive measures for Ticino: it reports the content of the question and the political problem posed to the Municipality. ## From the question to the prescribed threshold The most useful analysis contained in the parliamentary question is the comparison between the effects listed and the threshold required to activate the protections. The source does not present this assessment as already completed: it asks the Municipal Council whether the figures cited fall within the concept of “serious economic or social hardship” provided for by law. The point, therefore, is not merely to describe the presence of cross-border commuters, but to assess whether the impact referred to in the debate corresponds to the criterion indicated for the clause.
### The four steps of the parliamentary question | Step | Question addressed to the Municipal Council | |---|---| | Rules | Is it aware of the regional clause and the possibility of requesting its application? | | Assessment | Do the impacts fall within the concept of “serious economic or social hardship”? | | Pressure | Does it intend to ask the Council of State to turn to Bern? | | Refusal | What reasons would justify the decision not to intervene? |
The sequence separates four aspects: awareness of the provision, assessment of the situation, a possible formal initiative, and an explanation of a possible failure to act. The first question concerns awareness of the instrument’s existence; the second asks to link the problems indicated to the condition provided for by law; the third shifts the issue from the Municipal Council to the Council of State and then to the Federal Council; the fourth leaves open the possibility that the Lugano executive may take no action.
The reference to the FDFA appears in the section on the formal request: the parliamentary question asks whether the canton should assess specific measures for Ticino, as indicated by the FDFA. The source does not, however, list which measures would be adopted, nor does it report that a procedure has already been initiated.
The reference to the “figures cited” should also be read within the limits of the available material. No figures are reported for urban traffic, rents, wages, or social-services budgets. Therefore, the source allows the effects indicated by Wicht to be distinguished from an assessment of the legal threshold, but does not allow it to be established that this threshold has already been reached. The report documents a request for an assessment, not its outcome. ## The perimeter of the news The source does not attribute a choice already made to the Municipality. There is no response from the Lugano Executive, an intervention by the State Council, a decision by the Federal Council or the initiation of the application of the clause. The only explicit date linked to the instrument is September 2026, indicated for its approval in the question.
### No activation reported The relationship between the presence of frontier workers and local problems is also presented as the Wicht assessment. The source reports that, according to the city councilor, the phenomenon is reflected in traffic, rents, social services and wages. It does not add an autonomous verification, a series of quantitative data or an institutional decision confirming the application of the clause on the basis of these elements.
This distinction is relevant for the border worker and for those who follow the Canton of Ticino: the article talks about a possible regional measure provided for by the agreements between Switzerland and the European Union, not an already operational measure. The text also does not indicate individual consequences on a G permit, nor does it deal with AVS, LPP, LAMal, refunds, tax at source or double taxation. These themes do not appear in the four questions reported by the source; presenting them as effects of the clause would mean expanding the content beyond the news.
### What remains to be clarified The Municipality should therefore be asked to clarify three aspects already outlined in the question: whether it is aware of the new clause, whether it considers the situation described compatible with the notion of serious economic or social difficulty and whether it intends to urge the Council of State. If he decides not to move, the fourth question instead asks for a motivation to protect the residents of Lugano.
The source leaves all these steps open. It does not indicate what the response of the Municipality will be, whether the State Council will be involved or whether the Federal Council will consider measures for Ticino. The documented fact is therefore Omar Wicht's question and the institutional path it proposes, not the introduction of restrictions on frontier workers.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/lugano-durissimo-attacco-ai-frontalieri-per-colpa-loro-affitti-sempre-piu-alti-stipendi-bassi-e-disagi-per-il-traffico-urbano/)*

item.title: The long battle of cross-border workers: taxes, rights and disparities
item.description: About 31 thousand cross-border commuters in the Varese area and 32 thousand in the Como area Varese remains excluded from tax rebates after the return
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - About 31 thousand cross-border workers in the Varesotto area and 32 thousand in the Comasco area - Varese remains excluded from the rebates after the return to 4% - 31,7% spend more than an hour and a half traveling each day - 55,6% think they earn less than a Swiss resident
## Key facts - Workers involved: approximately 31 thousand in Varese province and 32 thousand in Como province - Tax rebates: approximately 4 million euros per year no longer received by Varese - Threshold: 4% in the ratio of cross-border workers to the population - Commutes: 31,7% spend more than an hour and a half per day commuting - Salary comparison: 55,6% lower than a Swiss resident performing the same duties
### The sequence of disputes In Varese province, approximately 31 thousand workers are involved; in Como province, 32 thousand. In recent years, for cross-border workers from the Varese and Como areas, the disputes have concerned taxes, rights and cross-border work rules. These issues begin with family finances and extend to relations between Italy and Switzerland and the budgets of municipalities in the border area.
At the center of the dispute is the so-called “health tax”: this contribution is предусмотрed for old cross-border workers and is strongly opposed by trade unions. The dispute has involved meetings and public initiatives, accompanied by announcements of legal challenges. The issue then became intertwined with the long-standing matter of tax rebates, that is, tax resources linked to cross-border workers, which represent an important source of revenue for many municipalities in the border area.
For Varese, the issue has had particular significance. Reinstating the 4% threshold in the ratio between cross-border workers and the population left the provincial capital without direct access to the funds. According to the source, this loss of access amounts to approximately 4 million euros per year, following the two previous years in which the provincial capital had received those sums.
The matter also concerns rights. The new tax regime introduced a distinction between “old” and “new” workers, adding complexity to an already complex system. In addition, there are the new unemployment benefit provided for by Law 83/2023 and teleworking, now among the central issues in discussions about the rules governing cross-border work. The matter therefore unfolds on several fronts: taxation, tax rebates, welfare, mobility and equal treatment. ## The daily cost of the border For 31,7% of respondents, the daily time devoted to commuting between home and work exceeds an hour and a half. The source refers back to this figure after describing queues at border crossings and long travel times: the commute thus becomes part of the same picture that includes salary, purchasing power, and equal treatment.
The research promoted by Cisl and Ocst, cited by the source, provides indicators concerning different aspects of the cross-border worker's experience.
### Five indicators to read separately | Indicator | Reported figure | |---|---| | Salary satisfaction | 73% satisfied | | Purchasing power | 48,4% believe they have lost it | | Salary comparison | 55,6% believe they earn less than a Swiss resident who performs the same duties | | Discriminatory treatment | 42,7% perceived it at least once as a cross-border worker | | Commuting between home and work | 31,7% spend more than an hour and a half a day |
The percentages do not measure the same thing. The 73% expresses satisfaction with salary, while 48,4% reports a perceived loss of purchasing power. The source does not present these figures as contradictory and does not attribute the loss to a specific cause. The 55,6% instead concerns the comparison with a Swiss resident who performs the same duties: it is a relative assessment, not the calculation of a salary difference.
The 42,7% should also be interpreted in its precise sense. It concerns those who report having experienced, at least once, treatment they perceived as discriminatory because they were cross-border workers; it therefore describes a perception reported by respondents, not an official finding. Taken together, the figures show that economic advantage does not encompass the entire cross-border experience. The source does not, however, indicate the total number of respondents, a data-collection period, the individual routes, or travel costs. It therefore does not allow these data to be turned into a calculation of the salary gap or the annual time lost commuting. ## The tax issue and the limits of the framework ### Dates and regimes not to be confused The source refers to a “new tax regime” and distinguishes between “old” and “new” workers. The verified reference for this matter specifies that the New Cross-Border Workers Agreement was signed on December 23, 2020, entered into force on January 1, 2024, and that the Italian ratification is Law 83 of June 13, 2023. Therefore, the phrase “new 2026 tax agreement” should not be used to indicate the entry-into-force date.
The same reference clarifies the distinction mentioned by the source. Cross-border workers who already had that status before July 17, 2023, benefit from an exemption of €7'500 under the 2024-2033 transitional regime. For new cross-border workers, the allowance is €10'000. On employment income, withholding tax is deducted only in Switzerland for cross-border workers; Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in section CE of form 730. The Italy-Switzerland Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation was signed on March 9, 1976, while Switzerland is not a member of the EU or EEA.
These elements help interpret the tax section without attributing the same withholding to both countries. However, the source refers to the Varese area, the Como area and municipalities in the border area: it does not break down the percentages by canton and does not present them as an exclusive statistic for the Canton of Ticino.
In addition, the amount of the health tax, the outcome of the announced appeals, the operational content of the teleworking rules and the details of the new unemployment benefit beyond the reference to Law 83/2023 remain undocumented. The text describes a long series of disputes, but does not indicate a common final solution. For the specific section on Ticino-Italy tax rebates, a dedicated in-depth analysis is available.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/la-lunga-battaglia-dei-frontalieri-tra-tasse-diritti-e-disparita/2713135/)*

item.title: The Lega calls for measures on cross-border commuters in Lugano
item.description: The strengthening was approved on September 29, 2026 Wicht asks the Municipality of Lugano to urge the Canton The request concerns the package
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The strengthening was approved on September 29, 2026 - Wicht asks the Municipality of Lugano to urge the Canton - The request concerns the Bilaterals III package - Traffic, housing, social services and wage dumping
## Key facts - Who: Omar Wicht, Lega municipal councillor - Where: Lugano and Canton Ticino - Article date: October 20, 2026 - Reference: Bilateral Agreements III and regional safeguard clause - Addressees: City Executive, Council of State and Federal Council
In the article published on October 20, 2026, Omar Wicht submits an inquiry to the Lugano City Executive concerning the new regional safeguard clause provided for in the Bilateral Agreements III package. The Lega municipal councillor wants to know whether the city executive intends to ask the Council of State to approach the Confederation to assess its application.
The reference is to the strengthening of the clause approved by the Council of States on September 29, 2026. The inquiry notes that the provision would allow Ticino to request targeted measures if serious economic or social difficulties were to arise.
### The situation described by Wicht The inquiry focuses on Lugano, the canton’s main economic hub, where Wicht points to a particularly large number of cross-border workers employed in the advanced tertiary sector and services. According to the municipal councillor, this concentration would affect traffic and housing costs, as well as place pressure on municipal social services and contribute to wage dumping.
Hence the request to clarify whether the situation in the area justifies intervention and whether the City Executive is willing to formally urge the cantonal government to act. The stated objective is to bring the matter before the Federal Council through the Council of State.
The questions follow four steps. The first asks whether the City Executive is aware of the clause and of Ticino’s explicit right to request its activation. The second asks whether the figures described as disproportionate in the submission constitute the serious difficulty required by law. The third concerns a formal letter to the Council of State requesting an assessment with measures limited to Canton Ticino, as provided for by the FDFA. The fourth asks for the reasons for any failure to intervene to protect Lugano residents.
The source text records the submission of the inquiry and the questions addressed to the City Executive; it does not report a response from the City Executive. ## From the request to a possible decision The report distinguishes between a request for assessment and an actual activation. Wicht does not announce the application of the clause; he asks the Municipality whether it is ready to write to the Council of State. The cantonal request, according to the intentions set out in the interpellation, should then be submitted to the Federal Council. The source does not say that the Municipality has already decided to proceed.
This sequence clarifies the scope of the initiative. Wicht does not claim that regional measures have already been introduced for Lugano or the Canton of Ticino. Instead, he asks for verification of whether the strengthening of the clause, approved on September 29, 2026, can be invoked for the territory of Ticino. In the document, the condition cited is the presence of a «serious economic or social difficulty»; the assessment of whether it exists is therefore placed at the center of the institutional debate.
### From the local level to the federal level | Step | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Municipality of Lugano | It is asked to clarify whether it intends to urge the Council of State. | | Council of State | It should be invited to submit the request to the Federal Council. | | Federal Council | It is the body to which the request for review should be submitted. | | Measures | They would be limited to the Canton of Ticino, as provided for by the FDFA. |
The relevant discussion for cross-border workers does not concern, on the basis of the source, a new individual rule. The interpellation links the presence of cross-border workers to a discussion of Lugano's economic and social conditions, in relation to traffic, housing, social services and wage dumping. However, it does not link the request to a change of contract, a new rate or a different social security scheme. The verifiable fact is therefore the opening of a political interpellation, not an immediate change in the cross-border worker's conditions.
The Confederation's role likewise remains envisaged rather than operational: the text speaks of the possibility of urging the Canton to submit the matter to the Federal Council. It does not describe a review already underway or a decision on the requested measures. ## The source's information limits The inquiry uses the expression “disproportionate numbers,” but the available text does not report counts, percentages, time series or other numerical values. The reader can therefore understand the criterion invoked, but cannot measure the weight of the situation or compare it with a threshold established by law. The source also does not specify what regional measures would be required: it refers to activation and measures limited to Canton Ticino, without describing their content.
No response from the Municipality of Lugano is documented. It is therefore not possible to say whether the city executive supports the request, rejects it or forwards it to the Council of State. Likewise, the text does not record an examination by the Federal Council, a decision by the Confederation or a timetable for any subsequent steps. These limitations distinguish the political proposal from its concrete effects on residents and workers.
### The scope for cross-border workers For those working between Italy and Canton Ticino, the source remains focused on the territorial dimension. It does not address the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax revenue sharing, withholding tax or double taxation. It does not mention INPS or Brogeda and does not refer to the expression “new tax agreement 2026.” Consequently, these topics cannot be used to describe the clause or to attribute changes in taxes, social security, insurance, border crossings or payslips to the request.
Regarding employment, the text is limited to indicating the high concentration of cross-border workers in the advanced tertiary sector and services and reporting Wicht’s assessment of wage dumping. In social and urban terms, it identifies traffic, housing costs and pressure on municipal social services as possible repercussions. The documented fact is therefore the inquiry reported on October 20, 2026; outside the content provided, both the Municipality’s response and any cantonal or federal follow-up remain to be verified.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/ticino/attualita/1957988/troppi-frontalieri-la-lega-chiede-di-intervenire)*

item.title: Cross-border workers: 55.6% receive lower salaries than residents
item.description: 1.542 responses collected from female and male workers 55,6% feel they are paid less than a Swiss resident The research will be presented on October
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 1.542 responses collected from female and male workers - 55,6% feel they are paid less than a Swiss resident - The research will be presented on 24 October in Varese - 73,2% mainly use a car for commuting between home and work
## Key facts - Survey: «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers» - Responses: 1.542 - Promoters: CISL dei Laghi, CISL Sondrio, CISL Piemonte Orientale and OCST - Scientific coordination: BiblioLavoro - Presentation: October 24, Centro Congressi Ville Ponti di Varese - Cross-border workers from Como: nearly 32 thousand - Cross-border workers from Varese: 31 thousand
On October 24, the study will be presented at Centro Congressi Ville Ponti di Varese. The event brings to the forefront the conditions of those who cross the border every day.
Entitled «Working across the border: conditions, needs and prospects of cross-border workers», the survey is promoted by CISL dei Laghi, CISL Sondrio, CISL Piemonte Orientale and OCST, with the scientific coordination of BiblioLavoro. The survey collected responses from 1.542 female and male workers.
Pay is among the main reasons for choosing Switzerland; however, according to the source, salary must be considered together with purchasing power, pay disparities, time spent commuting and a welfare system deemed inadequate.
### The salary comparison
The most prominent finding concerns pay: according to 55,6% of respondents, earnings are lower than those of a Swiss resident performing the same duties. This is the respondents’ assessment, referring to the same work activity indicated by the study, not a published salary figure.
### Mapping the phenomenon
Geographical origin provides a measure of the phenomenon observed. Nearly 32 thousand cross-border workers leave the province of Como, accounting for 41% of Italians employed in Ticino; another 31 thousand leave Varese.
These figures place the survey within the daily relationship between Italian territory and work in Switzerland, without reducing it to the paycheck alone. The starting point is a broad snapshot: salary drives the choice, while perceived fairness, travel time and overall conditions complete the picture submitted for discussion in Varese. ## The percentages considered together
The percentages in the research take on meaning when the questions they answer are considered. 73% of respondents say they are satisfied with their salary, while for 48,4% their purchasing power has decreased in recent years. The first number expresses an assessment of salary; the second, a perceived change over time. The source does not allow this gap to be interpreted as a causal relationship.
### A difference between groups
When compared with a Swiss resident who performs the same duties, 55,6% consider their earnings lower; among those without a collective agreement, the proportion reaches 63,4%. The two values differ arithmetically by 7,8 percentage points: the calculation shows the gap between the overall figure and the figure relating to a specific group in the research.
That calculation, however, does not prove that the lack of a collective agreement causes the perception of pay. The source does not analyze the reasons for the gap. Moreover, 42,7% report at least one treatment that, as cross-border workers, they perceived as discriminatory. The qualification «perceived» delimits the result: the respondents’ assessment is recorded, not a legal decision on the nature of the treatment.
### The cost of time and remote work
The commute exceeds an hour and a half per day for nearly one worker in three. 73,2% travel mainly by car. The research presents the two figures without publishing a table cross-referencing travel duration with the means of transport used: it is therefore not possible to know how many motorists belong to the group with the longest journey.
Another comparison emerges regarding teleworking. It is permitted for cross-border workers by only 37,4% of companies, while it is promoted by 95,2% of those who use it. The arithmetic difference is 57,8 percentage points, but the bases do not coincide: the first value concerns companies, the second those who already use teleworking. It therefore does not represent a measure of unmet demand in the entire sample. ## Welfare and the choice to remain across the border
The survey reports a clear result for the item referred to as “health tax”: 87,8% consider it disadvantageous. The expression in quotation marks is the one used in the source text. The same passage does not specify a technical name, an institution, an amount, or an insurance framework. The figure should therefore be presented as an assessment gathered by the survey, without turning the label into a technical definition of a tax or coverage.
76,9% of respondents rule out moving to Switzerland. According to the interpretation offered by the source, for the vast majority, cross-border work does not represent the start of emigration but a lasting choice. The percentage records a response to the survey: it does not document actual moves or explain the individual reasons for the choice.
Placing these two figures side by side does not make it possible to establish a cause-and-effect relationship between the assessment of the “health tax” and the decision not to move. They are two distinct findings from the same snapshot: one concerns an item considered disadvantageous, the other the prospect of moving to Switzerland.
### The information limitations of the snapshot
The document does not publish salary amounts, wage differences expressed in francs, individual cases, or a legal classification of the arrangements reported by cross-border workers. Nor does it break welfare down into individual benefits. For this reason, the percentages describe conditions and perceptions, but do not replace a complete measurement of the pay packet or of the rules applicable to each worker.
For the sake of precision, the material provided does not address G permits, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax, or double taxation. The reference to Italians employed in Ticino is not developed in a standalone section on the Canton of Ticino. These areas therefore cannot be presented as findings of the survey. Its scope remains that indicated by the title: conditions, needs, and prospects of cross-border workers.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/sui-frontalieri-pesano-le-disparita-uno-su-due-si-sente-pagato-meno-degli-svizzeri/2713108/)*

item.title: Scuola InOltre: twenty years of education in cantonal prisons
item.description: La Scuola InOltre turns twenty in 2026 Active since 2006 in the cantonal prison facilities In June, certificates were awarded to around thirty female
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The InOltre School turns twenty in 2026 - Active since 2006 in the cantonal prison facilities - In June, certificates were awarded to around thirty female inmates and nearly 230 male inmates - «Porte socchiuse» is scheduled for January 21, 2027
## Key facts - Project → InOltre School - Location → Cantonal prison facilities - Responsible body → Lugano-Trevano Technical Vocational Centre - Support → DECS and Department of Institutions - Recipients → women, men and minors - Offering → general education, vocational subjects, languages, IT and physical education - Certifications → bookbinding, IT and cantonal language certificates - Attendance 2025/2026 → around thirty female detainees and almost 230 male detainees
### An anniversary with an educational foundation
In 2026, the InOltre School celebrates twenty years of activity in the Cantonal prison facilities. The project provides learning opportunities and new perspectives even during detention; it is affiliated with the Lugano-Trevano Technical Vocational Centre and receives joint support from the Department of Education, Culture and Sport and the Department of Institutions.
The twentieth anniversary is part of an educational pathway launched in 2006. Since then, the offering has included general education, vocational subjects, languages, IT and physical education, along with practical and creative activities. It is aimed at women and men, including minors. Particular importance is given to certifiable skills: in bookbinding, both attestations and certificates can be obtained, alongside IT certifications and cantonal language certificates.
The latest figure concerns the presentation of attendance certificates for the 2025/2026 school year, which took place last June. The recipients were around thirty female detainees and almost 230 male detainees. Adding the two approximate figures, the indicative total is about 260 people: this is not a figure stated as an official total, but a calculation based on the rounded numbers available. The figure concerns that school year, not the entire twenty-year period.
For Marina Carobbio Guscetti, President of the Council of State and Director of DECS, education must be accessible to everyone, regardless of their circumstances. Norman Gobbi, Director of DI, noted that serving a sentence “goes beyond custody and security” and added that promoting reintegration also helps prevent recidivism. According to Gobbi, InOltre represents a unique model in Switzerland. ### Two formats for the twentieth anniversary
The initiatives for the twentieth anniversary will accompany the 2026/2027 school year. As far as can be inferred from the program, their common feature is not a single format: they range from collecting testimonies to educational work and, ultimately, to entering the cantonal prison facilities. Comparing the projects makes it possible to distinguish their intended audiences and expected results, without attributing effects to them that are not indicated.
The program also involves some classes from the CPTs of Lugano-Trevano and Mendrisio, which are tasked with examining restorative justice and reintegration in greater depth. The program will conclude with twenty students entering the cantonal prison facilities to give several lessons prepared during the year. The focus of the work, the number of students involved, and the final stage planned in the facilities are thus made explicit.
The difference between the two projects can be verified in their respective outcomes: a series of podcasts on the one hand, and lessons taught by the students on the other. The first brings together the voices of people who have encountered InOltre in different roles; the second plans a teaching presence in the cantonal prison facilities. Both accompany the 2026/2027 school year, but they are presented as distinct initiatives, with different participants, activities, and final results. ### Theatre and visual arts
The 20th-anniversary programme also includes a theatre course for incarcerated people, which began in September. The work will culminate in the «Half-open doors» event, scheduled for 21 January 2027 from 14 to 16 at the Cantonal Prison Facilities. The theatrical presentation will be intended for institutional and political representatives, members of the teaching staff and the media. This distinguishes it from the other 20th-anniversary events: it is neither a collection of interviews nor a lesson prepared by the students, but rather the presentation of a theatre work.
Alongside the theatre, an exhibition of works produced in the art mediation workshop has been set up at the CPT in Lugano-Trevano. Four murals created by incarcerated people are visible on the first floor of the facility. The exhibition thus adds a visible element to the 20th-anniversary calendar: the artistic production is presented at a CPT facility, while the theatre is located at the Cantonal Prison Facilities. The number of murals and the floor of the facility are specified precisely, with no further data on visitors or the content of the works.
These two elements show that the 20th anniversary is not concentrated in a single event. The theatre course has a presentation scheduled for January 2027, while the exhibition is already set up at the CPT in Lugano-Trevano. Thus, both an activity with a future presentation and an artistic presence already visible are documented. The programme also specifies a time slot and intended recipients from institutions, politics, teaching and the media for the «Half-open doors» event. The distinction between the locations is part of the framework: the theatre event is at the Cantonal Prison Facilities, and the exhibition at the CPT site in Lugano-Trevano. The calendar mentioned remains linked to the 2026/2027 initiatives and the exhibition already set up.

item.description: Accident at dawn on October 19 at Appiano Gentile Cars and motorcycles collide shortly after 6 Three people involved, one in serious condition
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Incident at dawn on October 19 in Appiano Gentile - Car and motorcycle collide shortly after 6 - Three people involved, one in serious condition - Ambulances, a medical car and an air ambulance activated
## Key facts - Date → Monday, October 19 - Time → shortly after 6 - Location → Via Salvo D’Acquisto, Appiano Gentile - Collision → a car and a motorcycle - Involved → three people - Severity → one person in serious condition - Emergency response → three ambulances and a medical response vehicle - Air ambulance → Villa Guardia base, red code
### The sequence of events still to be established
In Appiano Gentile, at dawn on Monday, October 19, a car and a motorcycle collided on Via Salvo D’Acquisto. The accident occurred shortly after 6, but the sequence of events preceding the impact has not yet been established: the source specifies that the causes are still being precisely determined. The location and time have therefore already been established, while a conclusive reconstruction of how the crash occurred is still lacking.
Three people were involved in the violent impact. One of them is reportedly in serious condition. This wording preserves the non-definitive nature of the health information reported in the account: the names, ages, or further details about the individuals and their injuries are not provided. The available information nevertheless makes it possible to distinguish the total number of people involved from the situation reported for one of them, without turning the latter indication into a more detailed medical bulletin than the source allows.
For now, the account of the incident ends with an issue still unresolved. On the one hand, the accident has already been located and placed in time; on the other, the causes and exact sequence of events remain to be clarified. The account assigns no responsibility, does not provide a definitive version of the collision, and does not report any subsequent developments regarding the condition of the person in serious condition. These omissions are not filled by speculation: in the available text, the reconstruction remains open.
The incident is described through a few certain but significant elements: two vehicles involved, three people affected, and a medical condition described as serious. The report remains anchored to what is stated in the source, without adding details that the account does not contain. ### The medical response and securing of the area
The report offers an interpretive element that goes beyond a simple list of vehicles: emergency management is described on two levels, medical and operational. On the former, Areu's operations center sent three ambulances and a medical car to the scene. It also activated the air ambulance, which took off from the Villa Guardia base under code red, defined in the source as the highest severity level. The list makes it possible to distinguish the ground response from the activation of the aircraft, but does not provide arrival times, hospital destinations, or clinical updates.

The second level concerns the accident scene. At the scene were the firefighters from the Como Command and the Carabinieri personnel from the Cantù Company. According to the report, the latter handled traffic management and carried out the technical surveys needed to reconstruct the exact dynamics of the crash. For the firefighters, however, only their presence is documented, with no further information on the activities carried out.

item.description: In September 2026 Italian prices rise by 0,7% monthly Italian inflation reaches 4,2%, from 3,3% in August Confindustria estimates 1% in 2026
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In September 2026, prices in Italy rise by 0,7% month on month - Italian inflation reaches 4,2%, up from 3,3% in August - Confindustria estimates 1% in 2026 and 0,6% in 2027 - The expected deficit rises to 3,4% of GDP in 2027
## Key facts - Italian prices → +0,7% month-on-month and +4,2% year-on-year in September 2026 - Inflation in Italy → 3,3% year-on-year in August - Euro area → 3,8% in September, up from 3,2% in August - Italian GDP → 1% in 2026, versus 0,5% estimated in March; 0,6% in 2027 - Deficit → 2,9% in 2026; 3,4% in 2027; 3,2% in 2028
In the data released on October 16, Istat recorded a 0,7% increase in the national consumer price index in September 2026 compared with the previous month and 4,2% year-on-year. In August, the annual change had been 3,3%. The acceleration weighs more heavily on household budgets and is centered on energy: the increase may be reflected not only in bills, but also in transport, industrial production and the distribution of goods.
### Italian and European prices
In September, according to Eurostat, the inflation rate in the euro area reached 3,8%, compared with 3,2% in August. The European picture therefore signals greater pressure, driven mainly by fuel and gas and, in part, by food prices. The tensions in the Middle East and difficulties in the energy markets cited by the source do not make it possible to determine how long the phenomenon will last. The impact will not necessarily be uniform across prices, but energy may gradually pass its costs on to numerous sectors.
### Growth and public finances
On October 14, Confindustria raised its forecast for Italian GDP in 2026 from the 0,5% estimated in March to 1%. The association attributes part of the resilience in the first half of the year to investments financed by European PNRR funds, which supported stronger-than-expected activity. For 2027, however, it forecasts growth of 0,6%; the reasons include the completion of the PNRR, rising energy costs and tighter financial conditions. This is a forecast, not a certainty, highlighting how part of the investment momentum depends on extraordinary resources.
At a parliamentary hearing on October 12, Banca d'Italia warned that deficits above 3% of GDP planned by the government for 2027 and 2028 could make it more difficult for Italy to exit the European excessive deficit procedure. Government estimates indicate a deficit of 2,9% in 2026, 3,4% in 2027 and 3,2% in 2028. Among the factors that, according to the source, weigh on the calculations are the increase in defense spending and measures connected with energy costs. ## The comparison that emerges from the data
The figures describe two distinct aspects: price acceleration and the growth trajectory. The Italian figure of 0,7% is monthly, while 4,2% and 3,3% are annual changes; they therefore do not measure the same interval. The change from 3,3% in August to 4,2% in September corresponds, as an arithmetic difference, to 0,9 percentage points. The euro area also moves from 3,2% to 3,8%, a difference of 0,6 points.
The source attributes the European increase mainly to fuels and gas, while for Italy it explains that energy can feed into transport, production, and distribution costs. The link described is therefore a gradual transmission of costs, not a forecast that every good will increase by the same amount.
### The growth trajectory
With regard to GDP, the time comparison is equally relevant. Confindustria's forecast for 2026 rose from the 0,5% estimated in March to 1% on October 14. For 2027, however, the same association indicates 0,6%. The difference between the two projected years shows a weaker pace after 2026, but does not constitute certainty about future developments. The relationship with the PNRR is identified by the source: investments supported by European funds contributed to the resilience of the first part of the year, while their completion makes it more important to understand which activities will be able to support demand afterward.
| Indicator | Initial period | Subsequent period | |---|---|---| | Italian prices, annual change | 3,3% in August | 4,2% in September | | Euro area inflation | 3,2% in August | 3,8% in September | | Italian GDP, 2026 forecast | 0,5% in March | 1% on October 14 | | Projected GDP | 1% in 2026 | 0,6% in 2027 |
### The Varese area
For the province of Varese, the source identifies a network of small and medium-sized manufacturing companies and many workers who commute daily. More expensive utility bills and fuel can reduce households' disposable income; for businesses, they increase operating costs. More expensive credit may also prompt some companies to postpone investments.
The effect is not uniform. It depends on energy consumption, the ability to pass costs on to prices, and customer demand. For those who travel every day, the text documents a possible impact on disposable income and businesses' economic conditions, but does not quantify individual spending, a paycheck, or a single journey. The local data should therefore be read as a description of pressures on households and businesses, not as a measure that is the same for every worker. ## Interest rates, budget and scope of the news
### The costliest financing
As Christine Lagarde, President of the European Central Bank, observed on 17 October, the recent rise in bond yields is increasing the cost of financing in the euro area. A tightening of financial conditions can slow economic activity and, by reducing demand, help contain inflation; at the same time, however, it makes credit more expensive for businesses and some loans for households.
For the ECB, the challenge is to keep inflation under control without excessively exacerbating the economic slowdown. An increase in interest rates does not directly increase the availability of gas or oil, but it can reduce the likelihood that an initial energy shock will spread to wages and the prices of other goods and services. Future decisions will be linked to developments in prices, the economy and expectations.
### The review of public finances
The relationship between exemptions from European rules and the excessive deficit procedure is at the center of the Bank of Italy's warning: such exceptions may prevent the launch of a new procedure for certain expenditures, but do not in themselves ensure exit from a procedure already under way. It will be for the European Commission to assess whether the improvement in the public finances will be lasting.
The issue for Italy is to balance public services, investment and support for households and businesses despite its high debt. The credibility of the budgetary path will therefore depend on the ability to make the improvement in the public finances lasting, in a context made more difficult by weak growth and energy costs.
### The measures indicated by the source
According to the source, these pressures have no single solution. In the short term, it points to transparency regarding energy offers and targeted support measures for those most exposed; over a longer horizon, it highlights energy efficiency, diversification of sources and the transformation of PNRR investments into lasting productive activities. For companies, monitoring cost trends and carefully planning investments can be useful, but it does not replace stable economic policies or a less uncertain international context.
For readers who work across the border, this distinction defines what can be attributed to the source. The text discusses the province of Varese and workers who commute daily, but provides no data on a cross-border worker, the Canton of Ticino or the border crossings. Also outside its scope are the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax and double taxation. These topics cannot be used to turn macroeconomic percentages into an individual change in salary, deductions or mobility.

## TL;DR - October 22, 2026: for MATCHING in Varese - From 9.00 to 12.30 at Ville Ponti - New report on the Varese labor market - Data, corporate crises and roundtable
## Essential details of the event - Event name → for MATCHING - Date and time → Thursday, October 22, 2026, from 9.00 to 12.30 - Venue → Andrea Hall, Ville Ponti Congress Centre, Piazza Litta 2 in Varese - Promoters → Province of Varese and Varese Chamber of Commerce - Document → “For Matching”: reading the data to address crises and support employment recovery - Target audience → institutions, businesses, social partners and industry experts
On Thursday, October 22, 2026, at the Ville Ponti Congress Centre in Varese, the Province of Varese and the Varese Chamber of Commerce will present the new Report on the labor market in the province of Varese. The meeting will examine how data can help interpret the labor market and address corporate crises.
The announced schedule runs from 9.00 to 12.30. Subtracting the start time from the end time, the planned overall duration is three hours and thirty minutes. The morning is therefore organized around two stages: the presentation of the document and the subsequent discussion among representatives from different fields.
### The document at the center of the morning
The report, entitled «For Matching: interpreting the data to manage crises and foster employment recovery», was created through collaboration between the two promoting bodies and falls within territorial policies devoted to action on industrial disputes and economic recovery.
The report aims to provide practical support for monitoring changes in the production system, identifying difficulties in advance, and guiding public and private strategies. The meeting aims to turn data analysis into concrete measures in support of employment and the competitiveness of the Varese area.
Once the data have been presented, the program provides for a roundtable with representatives from the institutional, economic, academic and trade union sectors. The meeting is intended for institutions, businesses, social partners and industry experts, who will discuss how to interpret the labor market and possible courses of action for the local production sector. ## From data to discussion
The most concrete relationship described by the source concerns the structure of the event. The new report is not presented as an isolated document: its presentation precedes a roundtable intended to pool institutional, economic, academic and trade union perspectives. The connection between the two moments is stated in the programme itself, without any need to attribute outcomes to the event that have not yet been reported.
### Three stated functions
| Step | Basis indicated by the source | Function of the document | |---|---|---| | Market analysis | Report on the labour market in the province of Varese | Interpret transformations in the production context | | Identifying critical issues | Local policies on industrial disputes | Detect difficulties at an early stage | | Guiding decisions | Economic and employment recovery | Guide public and private strategies |
The first function is interpretive: the report should help analyse changes in the production context, but the source does not indicate which transformations have emerged or which sectors are involved. The second concerns the timing of the analysis, since the text refers to the early detection of critical issues; it does not, however, say how many critical issues were identified or using which indicators.
The third function links the document to public and private strategies. Here too, the announcement describes the intended use of the publication, not decisions that have already been adopted. This distinction is useful to avoid confusing a report presented as an operational tool with an intervention plan that has already been defined.
The roundtable adds a second level. The discussion is not described as a vote or as the approval of specific measures. Its stated objective is to share perspectives and outline common lines of action to address the current challenges facing the local production sector. The documented value of the event therefore lies in the transition from analysing data to comparing different areas of expertise, while the outcome of the discussion remains entrusted to the morning’s proceedings. ## The scope of the available information
The announcement makes it possible to reconstruct precisely the organization of the event, but does not anticipate the numerical content of the new report. It indicates the title, the bodies that produced it, the area of reference and the operational purposes. It does not, however, report figures on employment, the number of industrial disputes, the production sectors concerned or the results already achieved.
### Participation and limits of the announcement
To participate, registration is required through the QR code on the poster or the event's online form; no further conditions apply. The event is scheduled for the morning of Thursday, October 22 and will be held in the Salone Andrea of the Ville Ponti Congress Center, at Piazza Litta 2 in Varese.
The composition of the round table is also described by category: institutions, the business community, academia and the trade union. The names of individual participants are not indicated. For the same reason, it is not possible to attribute statements, proposals or positions to people or organizations not named in the text.
The most significant limitation concerns the stage reached by the news. The source presents a scheduled event and explains that the report will be presented during the morning; it therefore does not report the outcome of the presentation or discussion. Based on the announcement, it cannot be established whether measures have already been identified, which public or private strategies were discussed, or what impact the proceedings had on employment in Varese.
The design of the initiative remains documented: using a snapshot of employment as the basis for targeted interventions, anticipating critical issues and bringing institutional, economic, academic and trade-union stakeholders together around the same table. These are purposes explicitly indicated by the source; the concrete results, however, can be assessed only on the basis of the report's contents and the outcomes of the round table, which are not yet reported in the announcement.

item.description: For the cross-border electrical designer in Ticino: agreement in force as of January 1, 2024, withholding tax only in Switzerland and different
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Agreement signed on December 23, 2020 - In force from January 1, 2024 - New cross-border workers: €10'000 tax allowance - Existing cross-border workers: €7'500 exemption, 2024–2033 regime
## Key facts | Term | Value | |---|---| | New Cross-Border Agreement | signed December 23, 2020; effective January 1, 2024 | | Italian ratification | Law 83 of 13 June 2023 | | Old cross-border workers | already such before 17 July 2023; exemption €7'500; regime 2024–2033 | | New cross-border workers | deductible of €10,000 | | Tax at source | held only in Switzerland | | Tax credit in Italy | CE framework of 730 | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% for the employee | | AD/AC | 1.1%; cap CHF 148'200 |
The new Cross-border Workers Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020, ratified in Italy with Law 83 of 13 June 2023 and is in force from 1 January 2024. For a cross-border worker who resides in Italy and works as an electrical designer in the Canton of Ticino, the sequence distinguishes three moments: signature, ratification and application. The operational date indicated by the source is January 1, 2024, not 2026.
The basic tax rule concerns withholding tax: the withholding of the income from work of cross-border workers occurs only in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation with the tax credit reported in the EC framework of 730. To read the pay slip, therefore, the Swiss withholding tax and the Italian credit are two elements to be kept separate; the source does not describe a full levy on the same income in both countries.
### The dates that affect the deductible
The distinction that changes the threshold is temporal. Those who were already such before 17 July 2023 are old cross-border workers: they are entitled to an exemption of €7,500, with a transitional regime from 2024 to 2033. New cross-border workers instead have an exemption of €10,000. The source links the threshold to the temporal category of the worker, not to the profession of electrical designer.
In the cross-border case, permit G also comes in. The geographical reference is the Canton of Ticino; Brogeda is among the crossings mentioned for the connection with Italy, but the source does not associate traffic data or different tax rules with the crossing. Permit, place of work and taxation remain distinct profiles: the first is administrative, the second follows the Swiss withholding and the Italian credit.
The Italy-Switzerland Convention against double taxation was signed on 9 March 1976. Switzerland is not a member of the EU or the EEA. This reference delimits the comparison between the Swiss and Italian systems without attributing to the profession a tax discipline different from that documented. ## From gross pay to payslip items
Comparing employment income in Switzerland with Italian tax rates requires separating periods, bases, and categories. The source distinguishes Italian IRPEF, Swiss contributions, and LAMal, which concerns health insurance.
| Item | Documented value | Period or basis | |---|---:|---| | Italian IRPEF | 23% up to €28'000; 35% from €28'001 to €50'000; 43% above €50'000 | 2024–2025 income | | Italian IRPEF | 23% up to €28'000; 33% from €28'001 to €50'000; 43% above €50'000 | From 2026; Law 199/2025, Art. 1 para. 3 | | AVS/AI/IPG | 5,3% | Employee share | | AD/AC | 1,1%; CHF 148'200 cap | Contribution indicated | | LAINF | 0,7–1,5% | Contribution indicated | | LPP | 7–18% | Age bracket, from the 25th year |
Between the two IRPEF rows, the €28'001 to €50'000 bracket goes from 35% for 2024–2025 income to 33% from 2026: two percentage points. The bracket up to €28'000 remains at 23%, and the one above €50'000 at 43%. This is a calculation based on the reported values, not a forecast of an electrical designer's net pay.
### Swiss contributions and LAMal
AVS/AI/IPG is listed at 5,3% for the employee. AD/AC is 1,1% with a CHF 148'200 cap. LAINF is 0,7–1,5%; LPP ranges from 7% to 18% by age bracket from age 25. The source does not present these items as a single tax rate.
LAMal is health insurance, not a tax on health. G cross-border workers have the right to choose; for adults, the deductible ranges from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. It should not be confused with the €10'000 tax allowance for new cross-border workers: the former is in francs and concerns LAMal, while the latter is in euros and concerns the tax treatment of the category.
For the Switzerland–Italy comparison, the withholding tax, IRPEF rates by period, and the listed contributions therefore remain available. Without gross pay, taxable base, and individual factors, the source does not allow the percentages to be converted into a net salary. ## Requirements and limitations of the available data
The material makes it possible to define the tax and administrative scope of the cross-border worker, but not a complete profile of the profession. No technical or professional requirements for the electrical designer are listed, nor is there a procedure for any recognition of the educational qualification. Nor is a salary range or pay difference with Italy reported. For this reason, the article can document the rules affecting how income is interpreted, without attributing to the role qualifications or amounts not present in the source.
### Entities that should not be confused
Withholding tax rates and federal and cantonal tax rates are established by federal or cantonal laws. At federal level, administration is the responsibility of AFC/ESTV, the Federal Tax Administration; at cantonal level, the cantonal tax administrations are involved. By contrast, the source excludes UFAS and BFS from setting the rates: UFAS concerns social security, including AVS/AI, while BFS performs a statistical function and collects data.
The distinction is useful when looking for a reference for the payslip. A social security institution should not be presented as a tax authority, and a statistical office should not be used as a source of tax rates. The role of AFC/ESTV concerns federal tax administration; the cantonal side remains linked to the canton’s tax administrations.
In the context of Ticino-Italy relations, tax rebates are also mentioned, but the source does not provide amounts, percentages or criteria for including them in the individual calculation of income. Similarly, the G permit is mentioned as a reference for cross-border work, without a detailed procedure in the available material. These limitations prevent the addition of undocumented administrative steps or salary figures.
### The data that remains verifiable
The dates of the Cross-Border Workers Agreement, withholding in Switzerland only, the Italian tax credit in Section CE of form 730, the exemptions for old and new cross-border workers, and the listed contribution rates remain verifiable. These are the data that link work in the Canton of Ticino to Italian-Swiss taxation. To organize tax items and withholdings in a simulation, tax calculator can be used.

item.description: Cross-border worker agreement, exemptions, withholding tax and contributions: the data to check when evaluating courses and professional retraining as

## TL;DR - The cross-border workers agreement has been in force since January 1, 2024 - Existing cross-border workers have an exemption of €7'500 until 2033 - New cross-border workers have an allowance of €10'000 - Employment income is taxed only in Switzerland
## Key facts - Signing of the agreement → 23 December 2020 - Italian ratification → Law 83 of 13 June 2023 - Entry into force → 1 January 2024 - Convention against double taxation → 9 March 1976 - Old cross-border commuters → €7,500 exemption, regime 2024–2033 - New cross-border commuters → €10,000 deductible - Tax credit → EC framework of 730 - Tax on earned income → only in Switzerland
The New Cross-border Workers Agreement was signed on 23 December 2020, which entered into force on 1 January 2024. The Italian ratification is Law 83 of 13 June 2023. For those seeking professional training or retraining in 2026, this chronology is the first check: the year 2026 does not replace the effective date indicated by the source.
The agreement distinguishes two audiences. Old cross-border workers, already such before 17 July 2023, fall under the transitional regime 2024–2033 and have an exemption of €7,500. For new cross-border commuters the indicated deductible is €10,000. The distinction should not be flattened into a single rule when evaluating the practical return of a path.
On earned income, withholding tax is only withheld in Switzerland. Italy avoids double taxation through the tax credit in the EC framework of 730. A description that attributes the same withholding tax to both countries would therefore be contrary to the verified data.
### The dates that separate the regimes
The 2026 new tax agreement formula can create a calendar error if it is read as the agreement date. The New Cross-Border Agreement dates back to 2020 and is in force from 2024. Even the Italy-Switzerland Convention against double taxation does not date back to 2026: it was signed on 9 March 1976. Switzerland is not a member of the EU or the EEA.
For a cross-border worker in the Canton of Ticino, the tax verification does not replace the verification of the training path. The source does not indicate courses, certification bodies, duration, costs, financing, access thresholds or reimbursement percentages. It therefore does not allow a course to be presented as recognized or financed, nor to quantify its economic return.
The checklist that can be derived from the facts is short. First the date of the cross-border relationship is set, then the old cross-border worker is distinguished from the new; the correct exemption or deductible is noted; finally, the Swiss withholding tax is separated from the Italian tax credit. If an evaluation adds tuition or reimbursement figures, those figures are not from the available material and should not be attributed to the source. ## Contributions and taxes: the correct comparison
The second common error is to read every deduction as if it were the same rate. The source separates Swiss contributions, health insurance and Italian tax. The available figures are as follows:
| Item | Verified data | |---|---| | AVS/AI/IPG | 5.3% paid by the employee | | AD/AC | 1.1%, with a CHF 148'200 cap | | LAINF | 0.7–1.5% | | LPP | 7–18% by age bracket, from age 25 | | LAMal | Adult deductibles CHF 300–2'500; right of option for cross-border workers with a G permit | | Italian IRPEF from 2026 | 23% up to €28'000; 33% from €28'001 to €50'000; 43% over €50'000 |
These figures cannot automatically be added together into a single percentage. The source presents them as separate items and, for AD/AC, also indicates a specific limit. There is no common basis for calculating an individual's net income or the financial return on a course.
AVS/AI/IPG, AD/AC, LAINF and LPP are Swiss contribution items. LAMal, by contrast, is health insurance: it is not a health tax. For cross-border workers with a G permit, the source recognizes the right of option and indicates adult deductibles from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500. This insurance figure cannot be converted into a training cost or financing.
The source also reports the Italian IRPEF rates from 2026 as 23% up to €28'000, 33% between €28'001 and €50'000 and 43% over €50'000, based on Law 199/2025, Art. 1, para. 3. For 2024–2025 income, the rates 23%/35%/43% are indicated. The direct comparison shows a difference of two percentage points in the middle bracket, but does not make it possible to calculate the overall tax without other data.
### Who sets the rates
Tax rates, including withholding tax and federal and cantonal rates, are set by federal or cantonal laws. At the federal level, they are administered by AFC/ESTV, while the cantonal tax administrations are also involved. They are not set by UFAS, which deals with social security, nor by BFS, which collects statistical data. Keeping periods, items and areas of responsibility separate avoids presenting as a course calculation a sum that the source does not permit. ## Limits and controls on retraining
The source also makes it possible to keep the names and areas of expertise of the institutions separate. AFC/ESTV and the cantonal tax administrations administer tax rates in accordance with federal and cantonal laws. UFAS is not the authority that sets withholding tax: its remit is social security, with AVS and AI. BFS does not establish tax rates, because it collects statistical data. Attributing a tax decision to these two entities would therefore be inconsistent with the available facts.
The acronym LAMal should be read as health insurance, not as a health tax. Cross-border commuters with a G permit are granted the right to opt, and deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2'500 are indicated for adults. Nor does the G permit provide, in the available material, automatic criteria for determining whether a course is recognized, funded, or economically useful.
With regard to training, the documentary limitation is clear. No specific courses, providers, certificates, recognition bodies, deadlines, funding amounts, or reimbursement percentages are identified. Nor is a numerical relationship between attending a course and an increase in salary documented. For this reason, the practical return can be indicated as an evaluation criterion, not as an already proven result.
The comparison supported by the source instead concerns specific scenarios: old and new cross-border commuters; transitional regime 2024–2033 and €10'000 allowance; entry into force in 2024 and reference year 2026; 2024–2025 IRPEF rates and rates from 2026; Swiss withholding tax and Italian tax credit. A faithful fact sheet can report these fields and leave out any data about courses that has not been provided.
The operational checklist therefore consists of setting the date, classifying the cross-border commuter, applying the correct exemption or allowance, separating taxation, contributions and LAMal, and verifying whether each training figure is actually documented. To relate the available data to salary, net pay and taxes, tax calculator is available.
